'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive]]
***A bridge between southern Ukraine and Russian-occupied [[Crimea]] has been damaged by a British-made [[Storm Shadow]] missile. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-65982817 (BBC News)]
*Eight people are killed and ten others are kidnapped after Islamic extremists attacked a group of farmers in [[Mafa]], [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/nigeria-boko-haram-farmers-killed-abducted-c67405c72d226ba2eadbe5c95854c432 (AP)] 
'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of Zambia]], [[China–Zambia relations]]
**[[Zambia]] [[Debt management plan|agrees]] with the [[Export–Import Bank of China]] and other [[creditor]]s to [[Debt restructuring|restructure]] [[United States dollar|US$]]6.3 billion in [[Government debt|debt]], which includes [[Maturity (finance)|maturity]] extensions and [[interest rate]] reductions. The deal, facilitated by the [[French government]], also allows Zambia to access a $1.3 billion [[bailout]] from the [[International Monetary Fund]]. [https://www.ft.com/content/e3b66798-1c5c-4c0c-8339-83a76e1e2c34 (''Financial Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Titan submersible implosion|''Titan'' submersible implosion]]
**The [[United States Coast Guard]] announces that they have discovered debris from the [[OceanGate]] submersible ''Titan'', which went missing while viewing the [[Wreck of the Titanic|wreckage]] of the [[Titanic|RMS ''Titanic'']]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-65993579 (BBC News)]
**All five people aboard the submersible are [[presumed dead]] after it was destroyed in an implosion. The [[United States Navy]] says that a sound they detected several days ago may have been the implosion. [https://www.reuters.com/world/search-intensifies-titanic-sub-with-only-hours-oxygen-left-2023-06-22/ (Reuters)] [https://www.insider.com/navy-detected-titanic-subs-implosion-soon-after-went-missing-wsj-2023-6 (Business Insider)]
*A fishing vessel sinks off [[Baganga]], [[Davao Oriental]], [[Philippines]], with two crew members found dead. Search operations are ongoing for seven others. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1792423/death-toll-from-fishing-boat-sinking-off-davao-oriental-climbs-to-2/ (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2023 Asia heat wave]]
**[[2023 China heat wave]]
***[[Beijing]], [[China]], reports a record temperature for June of {{convert|41|C|F}}, surpassing the previous June record of {{convert|40.6|C|F}} in 1961. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/beijing-braces-blistering-hot-weather-heatwaves-return-2023-06-22/ (Reuters)]
**It is announced that at least 170 people have died in [[Northern India]] due to the heat wave, with temperatures of up to {{convert|46|C|F}} reported. [https://www.dw.com/en/india-swelters-under-deadly-heat-wave/g-65991379 (DW)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[US Supreme Court]] rules in a 5–4 decision that the US federal government is not obligated to secure [[Navajo water rights|water access for the Navajo Nation]]. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/us-supreme-court-rules-against-navajo-nation-water-dispute-2023-06-22/ (Reuters)]
